Use case: lighting-weather / image relighting.
Edit the supplied original artwork in place. Preserve its aspect ratio, crop, camera, every subject, expression, pose, clothing panel, symbol, object, background layout and original drawn outlines. Do not reinterpret it as a new composition. Change only illumination, shading, existing highlights and existing material response. Preserve faces exactly in the original anime design with the same expression and feature positions; no added pores or new anatomy. Keep hands and fine clothing ornaments as drawn. Differentiate existing fabric, hair and metal by shading and highlight response, without adding textures or decoration. Preserve the source palette and medium.
Keep bright cores and clean edge gradients. Avoid smoothing hair locks, fine ornaments or costume linework, global fog, gray veil, uniform glow, clipped highlights, black crush and sharpening halos. Add or remove no objects, stars, fireworks, particles, visible light-source objects, decorations, text or watermarks.
Mode: Deep. Preserve all eight large characters AND the two tiny distant central figures, precisely their positions and gestures. Preserve the scrolling parchment, feather, balloons, field, existing musical staff, ribbons and original sparse cosmic background.
Current light evidence: gold parchment/central field illumination and cool blue musical light on either side. This is a strong cinematic RELIGHT of those existing objects, never cosmic world-building. Increase the warm golden environmental bounce on the characters' parchment-facing surfaces. Deepen clean readable shadows under existing hair locks, garment overlaps and contact points. Make source-supported cool blue edge highlights from the music trails more pronounced against warm-lit surfaces. Give the white-blue foreground character's existing dress folds deeper blue shading with soft highlights, retaining every panel and ornament. Make illuminated parchment regions more luminous but keep their original printed marks and color; opposing curved regions develop deeper readable amber shadows. Keep faces unclipped and readable. The difference in lit-versus-shaded surfaces should be clearly apparent at fit-to-screen size. Keep the original background's sparse stars and every existing firework exactly as depicted; don't amplify particle density or add nebulae, planets, galaxies, cloud banks or new effects.
